milestones.title: Choose the starting point
milestones.forecastNote: Download September 23; work starts September 24. Confirm call times across Kyiv/Bishkek, available study time, and device.
milestones.outcome: Student understands the goal, owns the setup steps, and has a feasible calendar.
milestones.demo: Explain the intended user flow and point to the next manual step; no existing application is expected.
concepts: C# is the language; MAUI is the application framework; XAML describes the UI.
A solution groups projects; a project produces an application or library.
Generated code is a learning aid: the student still runs and explains it.
milestones.teachBack: Which part of the application will open SMS, and who actually confirms sending?
acceptance: Meeting dates, available time, Android device/API and speech language recorded.
Project name chosen by the student, or explicitly recorded as pending before project creation.
Student can explain the planned SOS flow and locate setup instructions.

tasks.title: Confirm time, phone, language, dates, and current programming experience with the mentor
Explain the small application structure and record kickoff decisions without changing the source specification
Choose the project name and explain project name versus visible app title

milestones.title: First app and saved settings
milestones.forecastNote: Setup and first device deployment are the main schedule uncertainty.
milestones.outcome: The student launches their own project on Android and saves a phrase and contacts.
milestones.demo: Launch on the phone, change the phrase/contact, restart, and show saved values. Show one manually edited label.
concepts: XAML controls are connected to C# behavior.
Settings persist after the application closes.
Git diff shows a change; generated build files are not source code.
milestones.teachBack: Why does a saved phrase survive a restart while an ordinary variable does not?
acceptance: Student manually installed tools, created the named MAUI project under src, and launched it on Android.
Phrase, multiple contacts (add/edit/delete), SOS text, and channel settings persist locally.
Missing phrase/contact prevents starting Safety Mode.
Student changed a label manually and explained the relevant XAML/C# files.

tasks.title: Install Visual Studio and MAUI tools, create the named project, and run it on Android using student-setup.md
Inspect the student's scaffold; add suitable ignore rules and implement Home/Settings with local persistence and validation
Edit one UI label, run again, exercise contact CRUD, restart to verify persistence, and inspect the Git diff
Review changes, record checks and short explanations, and prepare Tuesday evidence

milestones.title: Prove offline speech early
milestones.entryCondition: M1-1 must be done; settings implementation need not be finished.
milestones.forecastNote: Critical technical gate. One focused diagnosis session if the experiment fails.
milestones.outcome: A verified speech approach on the target device, or an explicit blocker and mentor decision.
milestones.demo: With network disabled, recognize the chosen phrase after silence and unrelated speech, stop, and repeat.
concepts: Offline recognition means audio is processed on the device.
A speech session can finish before Safety Mode is stopped.
Device APIs can be unavailable even when the project builds.
milestones.teachBack: Why is recognizing a phrase once different from keeping Safety Mode usable after a pause?
acceptance: Device/API, speech package version, language availability, and repeatable results recorded.
No audio storage or online fallback in the chosen implementation; offline device behavior checked.
Silence, unrelated speech, repeat recognition, Stop, and microphone denial tested.
Foreground/lock-screen behavior agreed; unresolved failure blocks voice integration rather than being labelled success.

tasks.title: Implement a minimal offline speech experiment and inspect privacy/configuration; keep it small and reusable
Run the speech matrix on the physical phone, report outcomes, and explain offline versus online processing
Review feasibility and session behavior; record the selected approach or concrete blocker/options for the mentor

milestones.title: Complete the SOS path with a test button
milestones.forecastNote: Can proceed while S1 is blocked; report speech feasibility at this call.
milestones.outcome: Test SOS drives countdown, cancellation, real location, and a prepared SMS.
milestones.demo: Cancel one countdown; complete another and inspect the SMS recipient, location link, and timestamp without sending accidentally.
concepts: async/await keeps the UI responsive while waiting for the phone.
A state describes whether the app is idle, listening, or counting down.
Opening a message composer does not prove delivery.
milestones.teachBack: What must happen if the location result arrives after the student pressed Cancel?
acceptance: Five-second countdown, Cancel, and Send Now behave consistently and prevent duplicate opening.
Prepared SMS contains the selected recipient, message, real map link when available, and current timestamp.
Location denial/unavailability/timeout behavior is agreed and tested; coordinates are never fabricated.
Copy fallback works when message composition cannot be opened.
Speech gate result is available for the Thursday call, including blockers if any.

tasks.title: Resolve missing-location and recipient-selection rules with the student/mentor, then implement Test SOS, countdown, cancellation, and Send Now
Connect geolocation, message formatting, SMS composition, and copy fallback; test meaningful pure logic and state behavior
Change the default message manually; run Cancel, permission denial, SMS preparation, and fallback checks on the phone
Review SOS transitions and async cancellation; fix findings and prepare Thursday evidence including S1 status

milestones.title: Voice-triggered flow and both channels
milestones.forecastNote: Do not hide a failed speech gate behind Test SOS.
milestones.outcome: The real voice phrase starts the complete flow; SMS and WhatsApp are available.
milestones.demo: Start listening, say an unrelated phrase then the trigger, cancel once, repeat, and open the chosen channel. Show Stop.
concepts: A device event starts the same SOS flow as the test button.
Resources and pending operations must stop when Safety Mode ends.
milestones.teachBack: Why do the voice trigger and Test SOS call the same flow instead of duplicating its code?
acceptance: Start/Stop, visible listening state, recognized-text preview, normalized phrase matching, and voice countdown work.
Repeated detections do not create overlapping countdowns or message composers.
Agreed foreground/lock-screen behavior and restart rules work; Stop stops audio processing.
SMS and WhatsApp preparation, channel selection, recipient behavior, and missing-app fallback tested.
Student adds a small phrase-normalization test case manually and explains it.

WhatsApp opens the selected contact with encoded text, including +996 numbers and the agreed message language. The user confirms sending; recipients need no SafePhrase app. Opening the composer is not proof of delivery.

tasks.title: Integrate verified speech, normalized matching, session completion handling, Safety Mode state, and lifecycle cleanup
Add WhatsApp click-to-chat with international phone number and URL-encoded text; offer SMS/copy alternatives and manual sending, without bots or a messaging backend
Add one normalization test case manually; exercise the full voice flow, Stop, both channels, and repeated triggers on Android
Perform focused independent review of speech/privacy and SOS state transitions; fix findings and prepare Tuesday evidence

milestones.title: Package, verify, and explain
milestones.forecastNote: Run checks throughout development; reserve October 7-8 for final device regressions, fixes, and rehearsal. No speculative features.
milestones.outcome: An installable APK, requirement evidence, honest limitations, and a student who can explain the app.
milestones.demo: Install the APK, configure it, trigger and cancel SOS, repeat to prepare a message, then explain the main flow and one manual change.
concepts: Source code, build output, and an APK are different artifacts.
Tests provide evidence for specific conditions, not a guarantee for every phone.
The student can navigate settings, speech, and SOS flow without reading every line.
milestones.teachBack: Trace the safe phrase from its saved setting to the prepared message, naming the main responsibilities.
acceptance: AC-01 through AC-06 and FR-01 through FR-20 traced to recorded checks; any unmet requirement explicitly recorded.
Packaged APK installs and runs on the chosen Android device; signing/build configuration and reproduction steps documented.
Final review has no unresolved blocking findings; remaining limitations are listed for mentor review and no credentials or personal contact data are committed.
Student explains the flow, performs a small change, and describes privacy, offline, foreground, and manual-send limitations.

tasks.title: Complete the requirement/check matrix, fix device regressions, and write concise build/run/limitations notes
Build with guidance, install the APK, run the acceptance scenarios, and report real device results
Perform focused final review and relevant validation; prepare the candidate and an accurate final handoff
Rehearse the short walkthrough, explain the main responsibilities, and make one small change without generated replacement code
